cases.name: local_run_exit_status
cases.prompt: My CI script runs `torc run workflow.yaml` and it always passes even when jobs fail. Why?
assertions: states that torc run exits 0 even when jobs failed
recommends checking torc status or torc results list --failed
notes that torc exec exits non-zero on job failure

cases.name: slurm_submission_path
cases.prompt: My workflow has resource_requirements but torc submit says it has no schedule_nodes action. What do I do?
assertions: explains that torc submit requires a schedule_nodes action
uses torc slurm generate to produce an augmented spec
submits the generated spec rather than the original file
validates with torc create --dry-run before submitting

cases.name: node_sharing_capacity
cases.prompt: Our nodes have 104 CPUs and 240 GB. Each run needs 8 CPUs and 100 GB. How many runs share a node?
assertions: computes the minimum across CPU, memory, and GPU rather than CPU alone
identifies memory as the binding constraint giving 2 per node
notes that resource values are per node and integer division discards remainders
recommends verifying the declared memory against measured peak usage

cases.name: split_by_memory_and_runtime
cases.prompt: My Torc workflow mixes 100 small 20-minute jobs with 4 jobs needing 120 GB for 3 hours, and Slurm usage is enormous. Fix it.
assertions: explains that partition grouping sizes the group from the maximum of each dimension
splits the work with --group-by resource-requirements or per-job scheduler bindings
notes that the merged group forces the short jobs into the long walltime
quantifies or compares the resulting allocation counts
mentions strict_scheduler_match when a heavy job must not land on a light pool

cases.name: jobs_per_node_versus_more_nodes
cases.prompt: Should I pack more Torc jobs onto each node or request more nodes?
assertions: computes the per-node packing ceiling from resource requirements first
checks declared requirements against measured peak usage before adding nodes
checks whether the dependency graph is wide enough to use more nodes
warns that --max-parallel-jobs disables resource tracking entirely
recommends validating per-job runtime under the intended packing

cases.name: walltime_strategy_tradeoff
cases.prompt: I have 12 full-node one-hour Torc jobs on a 4-hour partition. Why does Torc plan 12 allocations and how do I reduce that?
assertions: explains time_slots as allocation walltime divided by job runtime
notes the default max-job-runtime strategy with a 1.5 multiplier yields one slot
recommends max-partition-time or a larger walltime multiplier
acknowledges the queue-priority tradeoff of a longer walltime

cases.name: single_large_versus_many_small
cases.prompt: 167 nodes of Torc work: one big Slurm allocation or many small ones?
assertions: runs torc slurm plan-allocations instead of guessing
explains backfill priority and fair-share degradation
notes that the many-small estimate covers only the first allocation
applies the answer with or without --single-allocation

cases.name: local_versus_remote_workers
cases.prompt: I want to spread this Torc workflow across three workstations over SSH. Anything to watch out for?
assertions: states that the server URL must be reachable from the workers, not just locally
notes that a standalone -s server cannot serve remote workers
notes that remote resource flags apply uniformly to every worker
mentions per-host output directories and log collection
mentions the per-host torc version check

cases.name: partial_rerun_choice
cases.prompt: Workflow 42 finished with 3 failed jobs out of 500 on Slurm. Rerun only those without redoing everything.
assertions: chooses a targeted reset such as torc jobs reset-status or torc recover rather than a full workflow reset
uses --dry-run before applying changes
explains that downstream dependents are reset by torc workflows reinit
resubmits with torc submit after the reset

cases.name: oom_diagnosis
cases.prompt: A Torc job on Slurm exited with 137. Diagnose it.
assertions: identifies 137 as SIGKILL, typically out of memory
corroborates with torc workflows check-resources --include-failed
checks Slurm state via torc slurm sacct or the dmesg log
recommends raising memory or running torc workflows correct-resources
does not assert OOM from the exit code alone without corroborating evidence

cases.name: runtime_blocked_packing
cases.prompt: Allocations are running with free CPUs but my ready Torc jobs never start.
assertions: runs torc workflows diagnose
explains that a job whose runtime exceeds remaining walltime will not be started
suggests more allocations, longer walltime, or lower job runtime
does not require Slurm access for the diagnosis

cases.name: json_parsing_shape
cases.prompt: My script runs `torc -f json jobs list` and jq fails with a parse error. Fix it.
assertions: identifies that the omitted workflow ID makes the CLI print a selection table on stdout
passes the workflow ID explicitly
notes that list commands return an object with an items array

cases.name: runner_log_filter
cases.prompt: RUST_LOG=torc=debug works for torc status but torc run ignores it.
assertions: explains that torc run installs its own logger accepting only a bare level
notes the Invalid log level fallback to info
recommends --log-level debug or RUST_LOG=debug for the runner

cases.name: api_change_chain
cases.prompt: I need to add a query parameter to an existing torc API endpoint.
assertions: edits src/openapi_spec.rs rather than api/openapi.yaml
runs api/sync_openapi.sh to emit, check, and regenerate clients
bumps HTTP_API_VERSION in src/api_version.rs for a new optional parameter
does not hand-edit generated client code

cases.name: pre_commit_gates
cases.prompt: What do I run before committing a Rust change to torc?
assertions: runs cargo fmt -- --check
runs cargo clippy --all --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
runs dprint check
notes that --all-features requires a database or the .sqlx cache
